slides: Let's continue, and see what happens when two things change.

slides.say: Now what if two things change at once? Then we multiply the factors, one after the other.
A printer prints ten pages a minute, for three minutes. Ten times three is thirty pages.
at: A printer prints ten pages a minute

slides.say: Now it prints twice as fast, and for four times as long. What happens to the work?
at: twice as fast, and for four times

slides.say: Twice the rate doubles the work. And four times the time multiplies it by four again. Two times four is eight. So the work is eight times as big.
Let's check it. Twice as fast is twenty pages a minute. Four times as long is twelve minutes.
at: Four times as long is twelve

slides.say: Twenty times twelve is two hundred forty. And thirty times eight is also two hundred forty.
A lot of students add the factors, two plus four, six. But each change multiplies what is already there. So we multiply.
Now one change that goes the opposite way. A team needs ten hours for a job. Now the job is three times as big, and the team works twice as fast.
at: A team needs ten hours for a job

slides.say: A bigger job takes more time. That's the same way, so the time is times three. Ten times three is thirty.
A faster team takes less time. That's the opposite way, so we flip the factor. Twice as fast means half the time. Thirty divided by two is fifteen hours.
at: Thirty divided by two is fifteen

slides.say: So for each change, ask one question. Does my answer grow, or shrink? The same way, we multiply as it is. The opposite way, we flip it.
at: The same way, we multiply as it is

slides.say: On the exam, a change in the rate often comes as a percent. Remember, a percent change is one multiplier.
A machine needs forty minutes for a job. Now it works twenty-five percent faster. How long does the job take now?
Twenty-five percent faster is times one point two five. And one point two five is five quarters.
The job is the same, so the time goes the opposite way. We flip the factor. Five quarters becomes four fifths.
Forty times four fifths. Forty divided by five is eight. Then eight times four is thirty-two minutes.
Careful, the time doesn't drop by twenty-five percent. Forty minus a quarter of forty is thirty. That's the trap.
at: Forty minus a quarter of forty

slides.say: So let's sum it up. Rate times time is equal to work. In the triangle, cover the one you want.
at: Rate times time is equal to work

slides.say: A rate is per one unit of time, and the units must match.
at: A rate is per one unit

slides.say: When the time or the rate is fixed, the other two move the same way.
at: When the time or the rate

slides.say: When the work is fixed, the rate and the time move opposite ways.
And with two changes, we multiply the factors. A factor that goes the opposite way gets flipped.

slides: Take a moment to memorize this. Now try the first question, and I'll see you in the next video.
